parts.text:
34 A student describes potential difference as the energy transferred per unit charge.
Which statement about the energy transfer is correct?
A
It is from electrical energy into other forms.
B
It is from other forms into electrical energy.
C
It only takes place inside a power supply.
D
It only takes place inside resistors.

hints: Notice the question says potential difference, not e.m.f. - recall which term applies across a load and which applies across a source.
Recall $V = W/Q$ for potential difference, where $W$ is the electrical energy converted to other forms per charge $Q$ in coulombs.
Compare the direction of conversion: ask whether charge is losing electrical energy to the component or gaining it from a chemical or other store.
walkthrough: Identify the definition being tested: the student defines potential difference as energy transferred per unit charge, $V = W/Q$.
State the rule: potential difference $V$ across a component is the electrical energy $W$ transferred out of the circuit into other forms per unit charge passing through.
Contrast with e.m.f. $E$: e.m.f. is the other-way transfer where non-electrical energy inside a power supply is converted into electrical energy per unit charge.
Check location: potential difference drops occur in the external circuit across loads such as lamps, heaters and resistors, not only inside the supply and not only in resistors.
Therefore the transfer for potential difference is from electrical energy into other forms. This is option A.

A.explanation: Potential difference is the electrical energy lost per unit charge when charge passes through a load, so it is from electrical energy into heat, light or other forms.

B.explanation: Transfer from other forms into electrical energy describes e.m.f. of a source, not potential difference across a component.

C.explanation: Energy supplied inside a power supply is e.m.f., whereas potential difference is measured across components outside the supply.

D.explanation: Potential difference occurs across any load such as lamps and motors, not only inside resistors.
